items.headline: Greed falls to 63 while Valuation stays at 86; PRICE_DISCIPLINE remains active
items.summary: The AGCI live engine reads Greed 63/100, down 7 points day over day and 24 points over seven days, while Valuation remains 86/100. The regime is Correction and the matrix condition remains PRICE_DISCIPLINE — Wait / Price discipline.
items.whyItMatters: Risk appetite is resetting materially faster than valuation. This improves future entry optionality but does not yet justify broad beta expansion while aggregate valuation remains extreme.

items.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics / Reuters
items.headline: August CPI rises 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y; core rises 0.3% m/m and 2.4% y/y
items.summary: August U.S. consumer prices increased 0.4% month over month and 3.4% year over year, with gasoline contributing to the monthly acceleration. Core CPI rose 0.3% month over month and 2.4% year over year. The release reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve may need to tighten again at its September meeting.
items.whyItMatters: Inflation is no longer falling cleanly into the energy shock. Combined with oil above USD 100 and firm producer prices, the hurdle rate for duration and long-duration equities remains high.
items.agciSignal: CPI FIRM / FED HIKING RISK UP / DURATION DISCIPLINE

items.headline: IEA warns the 2026 oil supply gap is widening as normal Gulf flows remain delayed
items.summary: The IEA now expects a materially deeper 2026 supply shortfall as Gulf disruptions persist. Reuters reports Saudi output around 6 million barrels per day, its lowest in decades, while diesel prices and refined-product tightness remain severe. Brent is still above USD 100 despite intraday easing on diplomatic headlines.
items.whyItMatters: The energy shock is broadening from shipping risk into sustained production and refined-product constraints. That raises the probability of second-round inflation and keeps a moderate energy hedge relevant, while making late-cycle oil chasing increasingly dangerous.
items.agciSignal: GULF SUPPLY GAP / DIESEL TIGHTNESS / INFLATION TAIL RISK

items.headline: Mexico and Washington accelerate bilateral trade talks ahead of U.S. midterms
items.category: Mexico / USMCA / Trade / Industrial Real Estate
items.summary: Mexico and the United States are pushing to reach an interim bilateral trade arrangement before the November U.S. elections. Discussions include relief from selected tariffs in exchange for stronger U.S.-content requirements and tighter scrutiny of Chinese investment, with Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminum and autos among the key unresolved issues.
items.whyItMatters: This is the first new trade development in several cuts strong enough to alter the Mexico watch. A workable interim arrangement could improve nearshoring confidence, but tighter content rules may redistribute winners across autos, industrial parks and supply chains rather than lift all Mexico exposure equally.
items.agciSignal: USMCA NEGOTIATION MOMENTUM / SELECTIVE NEARSHORING UPSIDE / CONTENT-RULE RISK

items.newsletter: Oracle earnings / Barron's Daily Roundup / 10-11 Sep 2026
items.headline: Oracle backlog reaches USD 664 billion while customer prepayments reduce the near-term capital burden
items.summary: Oracle reported more than USD 30 billion of new AI cloud contracts and total backlog of USD 664 billion. First-quarter capex reached USD 28.5 billion, but customer prepayments and customer-supplied chips reduced the effective funding burden; negative free cash flow was materially better than expected.
items.whyItMatters: This is positive evidence for the AGCI AI-quality framework because contracted demand is increasingly paired with customer funding. The remaining question is whether backlog converts on schedule without excessive leverage, project delays or margin dilution.
items.agciSignal: AI BACKLOG QUALITY IMPROVES / CUSTOMER FUNDING / LEVERAGE STILL MATTERS

items.newsletter: Adobe earnings / Barron's Daily Roundup / 10-11 Sep 2026
items.headline: Adobe beats on AI-driven demand, but softer forward revenue keeps competitive risk visible
items.summary: Adobe reported quarterly revenue of USD 6.76 billion, above expectations, with annual recurring revenue from AI-first offerings more than doubling year over year. However, the midpoint of its next-quarter revenue outlook was slightly below consensus and the shares fell after hours.
items.whyItMatters: AI monetization is becoming visible in software, but strong AI engagement does not automatically protect valuation or competitive position. AGCI should distinguish real recurring revenue from multiple expansion and watch pricing power versus newer design platforms.
items.agciSignal: AI SOFTWARE MONETIZATION / COMPETITION TEST / MULTIPLE DISCIPLINE
